[![Launch in Binder](https://mybinder.org/badge_logo.svg)](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/CaltechExperimentalGravity/system_ident/HEAD?urlpath=lab/tree/docs/examples/01-single-resonance.ipynb)  ·  run this page live (no install; the [in-browser demo](interactive.qmd) is instant)

The smallest complete **Pintelon–Schoukens** experiment: a simple harmonic oscillator
at 1 Hz with Q = 20, identified end-to-end and shown through the **full diagnostic
set** every example in this book uses — excitation design, the measurement time series,
a magnitude/phase/coherence Bode stack, fit residuals, parameter recovery against the
Cramér–Rao bound, drive-safety margins, convergence, and a pass-by-pass view of the
measurement sharpening.

The pipeline is always the same three moves, run for several passes:

1. **design** an optimal periodic multisine that puts drive power where the model is
   most uncertain;
2. **measure** the frequency-response function (FRF) leakage-free with a synchronous,
   integer-period DFT;
3. **fit** the plant by maximum likelihood, weighting each bin by its measured
   uncertainty — then redesign from the improved model and repeat.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Setup — imports, house plot style, plant & prior"
import sys, pathlib
_p = pathlib.Path.cwd()
for _c in [_p, *_p.parents]:
    for _d in (_c, _c / "docs"):
        if (_d / "sysid_plots.py").exists() and str(_d) not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, str(_d))

import numpy as np
import sysid_plots as sp
from sysid_campaign import run_siso_passes, param_sigmas, param_convergence_series

from system_ident.model import TFModel
from system_ident.fisher import parameter_covariance
from system_ident.design.pintelon import prior_robust_excitation, optimal_excitation
from system_ident.backends.twin import TwinBackend
from system_ident.plant import SuspensionPlant

# ── experiment geometry ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# NPERSEG/FS sets the analysis window T_fft; keep T_fft > 3/f_min for resolution.
FS, NPERSEG, N_PERIODS = 32.0, 4096, 6            # T_fft = 128 s, df ≈ 0.008 Hz
TOTAL = NPERSEG * N_PERIODS / FS
FMIN, FMAX = 0.2, 8.0
ACT_LIMIT = 1000.0                                # actuator saturation [cts]

# Synchronous DFT grid: every multisine line lands exactly on a bin -> leakage-free.
f_all = np.fft.rfftfreq(NPERSEG, 1 / FS)
band  = (f_all >= FMIN) & (f_all <= FMAX)
freq  = f_all[band]

# ── plant and prior ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
true  = TFModel.from_resonances([(1.0, 20.0)],  gain=100.0)  # 1 Hz, Q = 20
prior = TFModel.from_resonances([(0.95, 18.0)], gain=110.0)  # 5% off f0, 10% off Q

Pyy    = np.ones_like(freq)          # white readout-noise floor
Px_tot = 1.0                         # fixed drive-power budget
```

## The parameters being recovered

Every step below reprints this table, so the numbers can be followed pass by pass. The
campaign starts from the **prior** alone — deliberately wrong by 5 % in $f_0$, 10 % in $Q$.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Prior vs true parameters"
f0t, Qt = sp.f0_q(true);  f0p, Qp = sp.f0_q(prior)
sp.param_table(
    ["", "f₀ [Hz]", "Q", "DC gain |G(0)|"],
    [["prior", f"{f0p:.4f}", f"{Qp:.2f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(prior):.4g}"],
     ["true",  f"{f0t:.4f}", f"{Qt:.2f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(true):.4g}"]],
    caption="Before measuring")
```

## 1 — Design the excitation

The optimal drive is the fixed point of the Pintelon–Schoukens dispersion function:
it pours power into the bins that carry the most Fisher information about $(f_0, Q)$ —
the resonance and its skirts — instead of spreading it flat. **Same total power, sharper
parameters.** The first pass uses a prior-robust drive (spread over $f_0(1\pm u)$) so a
far prior still covers the true resonance.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Design the prior-robust drive; quantify the variance win"
Pxx_opt  = prior_robust_excitation(freq, prior, Pyy, Px_tot, 0.5, n_iter=6)
Pxx_flat = np.full_like(freq, Px_tot / (freq[-1] - freq[0]))

cov_opt  = parameter_covariance(freq, true, Pxx_opt,  Pyy, TOTAL)
cov_flat = parameter_covariance(freq, true, Pxx_flat, Pyy, TOTAL)
ratio    = np.max(np.diag(cov_flat)) / np.max(np.diag(cov_opt))

sp.excitation_design(
    freq, np.abs(true.eval(freq)), np.sqrt(Pxx_opt), np.sqrt(Pxx_flat),
    prior_mag=np.abs(prior.eval(freq)), ratio=ratio,
    annotations=[(1.0, "f₀ = 1.0 Hz, Q = 20")]).show()
```

::: {.callout-note}
The variance reduction above yields tighter parameters at **no extra measurement time or
drive power**, from a different allocation of the same budget. That is what optimal
experiment design provides.
:::

## 2 — Run the campaign

Three passes of design → inject → leakage-free FRF → inverse-variance accumulate → ML
refit. The first pass is the prior-robust drive; later passes are point-optimal from the
improving model.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Run 3 passes of Pintelon–Schoukens refinement"
tw = TwinBackend(SuspensionPlant({"POS": true}, FS),
                 {"C1:EXC": "POS"}, {"C1:RSP": "POS"}, fs=FS, sensor_asd=5e-3)

hist = run_siso_passes(tw, "C1:EXC", "C1:RSP", prior, fs=FS, nperseg=NPERSEG,
                       n_periods=N_PERIODS, band=band, freq=freq, Pyy=Pyy,
                       px_total=Px_tot, n_passes=3, prior_uncertainty=0.5, seed=0)
final = hist[-1]["model"]
```

The parameters at every pass — converging onto the truth:

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Parameter evolution: prior → each pass → true"
rows = [["prior", f"{f0p:.4f}", f"{Qp:.2f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(prior):.4g}", "—"]]
for h in hist:
    f0, Q = sp.f0_q(h["model"])
    rows.append([f"pass {h['pass']}", f"{f0:.4f}", f"{Q:.2f}",
                 f"{sp.dc_gain(h['model']):.4g}", f"{h['frac']:.2e}"])
rows.append(["true", f"{f0t:.4f}", f"{Qt:.2f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(true):.4g}", "—"])
sp.param_table(["step", "f₀ [Hz]", "Q", "DC gain |G(0)|", "σ/θ (CRB)"], rows,
               caption="Parameters at each step")
```

## ▶ The loop converging

Press **Play** for six passes of the loop: the drive ASD (bottom) reallocates power
toward the resonance while the maximum-likelihood fit (top, gold dashed) tightens onto the
true plant. The slider steps through the passes individually.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Animated convergence over passes"
anim = run_siso_passes(tw, "C1:EXC", "C1:RSP", prior, fs=FS, nperseg=NPERSEG,
                       n_periods=N_PERIODS, band=band, freq=freq, Pyy=Pyy,
                       px_total=Px_tot, n_passes=6, prior_uncertainty=0.5, seed=1)
sp.animate_passes(freq, np.abs(true.eval(freq)),
    [dict(meas_mag=np.abs(h["H"]), mask=h["mask"],
          fit_mag=np.abs(h["model"].eval(freq)), drive_asd=np.sqrt(h["Pxx"]))
     for h in anim]).show()
```

## 3 — Is the drive gentle? The measurement time series

The Schroeder phasing gives the multisine a low crest factor: a smooth, bounded waveform
rather than an impulsive kick. The mirror settles into a steady bounded oscillation: the
suspension is driven smoothly rather than stepped.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Drive + mirror motion, first ~64 s of pass 1"
t = np.arange(int(64 * FS)) / FS
sp.timeseries(
    t,
    [("drive (POS actuator)", hist[0]["drive"], sp.SKY)],
    [("mirror motion", hist[0]["response"], sp.GOLD)],
    titles=["<b>Drive</b> — POS actuator (Schroeder multisine)",
            "<b>Mirror motion</b> — response at the 1 Hz mode"]).show()
```

## 4 — Bode: magnitude, phase, and coherence

The accumulated leakage-free FRF (grey points, ±σ from period-to-period scatter), the
prior we started from, and the maximum-likelihood fit, against the true plant. Power is
concentrated at the resonance, so that is where the measurement is densest, the coherence
is highest, and the fit is pinned.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Magnitude / phase / coherence stack"
mask = hist[-1]["mask"]
sp.bode(freq, [
    dict(name="true plant",        H=true.eval(freq),  color=sp.SKY,  width=2.6),
    dict(name="measured (±σ)",     H=hist[-1]["H_acc"],
         color=sp.GRAY, mode="markers", err=hist[-1]["err_acc"], mask=mask),
    dict(name="prior",             H=prior.eval(freq), color=sp.RED,  dash="dot"),
    dict(name="ML fit",            H=final.eval(freq),  color=sp.GOLD, dash="dash"),
], coh=hist[-1]["coh"], coh_mask=mask).show()
```

## 5 — Fit residuals

A well-specified maximum-likelihood fit leaves residuals $(\,\hat H-G)/\sigma$ scattered
in $\pm\sim$2 with no frequency structure, and a near-standard-normal histogram. Structure
here would betray an unmodeled mode or a wrong noise model.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Normalized residual + histogram"
resid = ((hist[-1]["H_acc"] - final.eval(freq)) / hist[-1]["err_acc"]).real
sp.residuals(freq, resid, mask).show()
```

## 6 — Parameter recovery against the Cramér–Rao bound

Prior → fit → true for each parameter, with the error bar on the fit taken from the
**accumulated CRB covariance** (propagated to $f_0$, $Q$, gain). The fit lands on the
truth well inside its uncertainty.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Parameter recovery with CRB error bars"
f0f, Qf = sp.f0_q(final)
sig = param_sigmas(final, hist[-1]["cov"])
sp.parameter_recovery([
    dict(label="f₀ [Hz]",        prior=f0p, fit=f0f, true=f0t, sigma=sig["f0"]),
    dict(label="Q",              prior=Qp,  fit=Qf,  true=Qt,  sigma=sig["Q"]),
    dict(label="DC gain |G(0)|", prior=sp.dc_gain(prior), fit=sp.dc_gain(final),
         true=sp.dc_gain(true), sigma=sig["gain"], log=True),
]).show()
print(f"recovery error:  f0 {100*abs(f0f-f0t)/f0t:.2f}%   Q {100*abs(Qf-Qt)/Qt:.2f}%")
```

## 7 — Drive-safety margins

The peak drive and readback RMS at each pass, against the actuator-saturation limit. The
optimal excitation stays far inside the limit — safe to run on real hardware.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Drive peak & RMS vs the actuator limit, per pass"
sp.saturation([{"pass": h["pass"], "peak": h["peak"], "rms": h["rms"]} for h in hist],
              limit=ACT_LIMIT).show()
```

## 8 — Convergence — every parameter

Fractional uncertainty $\sigma_i/\theta_i$ from the accumulated CRB, pass by pass, for
**each** parameter — not just the worst. The loop stops when all of them clear target.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "σᵢ/θᵢ vs pass, per parameter"
sp.convergence(param_convergence_series(hist, ["f0", "Q", "gain"], ["f₀", "Q", "gain"]),
               target=0.05).show()
```

## 9 — Pass-by-pass: the measurement sharpening

Each pass redesigns the drive from the improved model and folds its leakage-free FRF into
the inverse-variance accumulator. The measured points and the fit tighten onto the true
plant as passes accumulate (color ramps blue → gold).

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Measured FRF + fit, overlaid per pass"
sp.pass_overlay(freq,
    [dict(meas_mag=np.abs(h["H"]), fit_mag=np.abs(h["model"].eval(freq)),
          mask=h["mask"]) for h in hist],
    np.abs(true.eval(freq))).show()
```

## 🎛 Interactive resonance

Dragging the sliders updates the Bode magnitude of a second-order resonance in the
browser (no server, no re-run). $f_0$ slides the peak; raising $Q$ makes it taller
and sharper. This is the shape the loop above is built to measure.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| panel: input
viewof f0 = Inputs.range([0.3, 3.0], {value: 1.0, step: 0.01, label: "f₀  [Hz]"})
viewof Q  = Inputs.range([2, 80],   {value: 20,  step: 1,    label: "Q"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
bode = {
  const w0 = 2 * Math.PI * f0;
  const data = d3.range(0.1, 5.0001, 0.01).map(f => {
    const w = 2 * Math.PI * f;
    const re = w0 * w0 - w * w;
    const im = w0 * w / Q;
    return { f, mag: (w0 * w0) / Math.hypot(re, im) };   // DC-normalized, |G(0)| = 1
  });
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 820, height: 380, marginLeft: 64, marginBottom: 52,
    x: { type: "log", label: "Frequency  [Hz] →", grid: true },
    y: { type: "log", label: "↑ |G(f)|", grid: true, domain: [0.02, 100] },
    style: { fontFamily: "Outfit, Inter, sans-serif", fontSize: "15px" },
    marks: [
      Plot.areaY(data, { x: "f", y: "mag", fill: "rgba(31,138,192,0.10)" }),
      Plot.line(data, { x: "f", y: "mag", stroke: "#1F8AC0", strokeWidth: 3 }),
      Plot.ruleX([f0], { stroke: "#C8973A", strokeDasharray: "5,4", strokeWidth: 2 }),
      Plot.text([{ f: f0, mag: Q }], {
        x: "f", y: "mag", text: [`f₀ = ${f0.toFixed(2)} Hz,  Q = ${Q}`],
        dy: -12, fill: "#C8973A", fontWeight: 700, fontSize: 14 }),
    ],
  });
}
```
